figures.caption: Fig. 1: Effectiveness of diversity-aware view partitioning, (a) Our method reconstructs more geometrically consistent structures while preserving finer scene details compared to existing efficient VGGT variants, such as LiteVGGT [32]. (b) Unlike other methods [32, 40], whose performance tends to degrade as the number of input frames increases, our simple diversity-aware view partitioning mitigates this effect and achieves a better efficiency–accuracy trade-off.

Fig. 2: Impact of frame count on VGGT performance. Red boxes indicate high-error regions where VGGT struggles with many frames, while green boxes indicate low-error regions. Frames sampled from each region show that failures occur in visually redundant views, whereas successful regions exhibit greater viewpoint diversity.

Fig. 4: Overview of the proposed framework. Input frames are first partitioned using visual dissimilarity. A selected reference chunk is processed by VGGT to obtain pseudospatial cues, which are used to estimate pseudo-poses for the remaining frames. The frames are then reorganized into balanced chunks that maximize both visual and spatial diversity, and each chunk is processed independently by VGGT.
